JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental case: Q1 2026 revenue of $49.84B (+10% YoY), EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY), and net income of $16.49B (+12.6% YoY) demonstrate genuine operating leverage across CIB (revenue +19%), Markets (+20%), and IB fees (+28%). The franchise is best-in-class — #1 in retail deposits, credit cards, and global IB fees for 17 consecutive years, with $7.1T in client assets and $40B in excess capital (CET1 14.3%). Valuation is the most compelling quantitative signal: P/E of 13.85x sits at/near the floor of its 365-day range (13.9–17.8x), having compressed ~20% from 17.3x in early January while earnings accelerated. P/B at 2.24x is likewise at the floor of its 2.2–2.8x range. The earnings yield of 7.2% offers a ~273bp equity-risk premium over the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%. This divergence — rising earnings, falling multiples — is the core setup. The score is capped below +0.5 by material macro headwinds: oil at $104.66/bbl (+67%), 10-year yields surging to 4.47% (+10.4% over 90 days), yield-curve flattening (10Y-2Y at 0.47%), and Basel III endgame potentially requiring ~$20B in additional capital by 2028. Card NCO guidance of ~3.4% signals credit normalization, and expense growth of 14% YoY outpaced revenue ex-Markets. No clear near-term dated catalyst exists to trigger a re-rating — Q1 already printed and the next earnings event is months away. The score reflects a high-quality franchise at a historically cheap multiple, tempered by genuine macro and regulatory uncertainty.
